subject: gk
question: Which of the following commissions is NOT a statutory body in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Commission for Farmers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Commission for Farmers** is NOT a statutory body in India, as it was formed through an executive resolution rather than legislation.
 
• It was constituted in **November 2004** under the chairmanship of Dr. M.S. Swaminathan to address issues related to farmers' welfare.
 
• Unlike other commissions such as the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) or National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST), it lacks a legal framework or statutory mandate.
 
• Statutory bodies are established by an act of Parliament and have defined powers and functions, which the National Commission for Farmers does not possess.
 
• The commission primarily serves as an advisory body, providing recommendations for improving agricultural practices, farmers’ income, and rural development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Statutory Bodies:**

 
 
• These are established by an act of Parliament or state legislatures.
 
• Examples include the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) and the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST).
 
• They have clearly defined powers, functions, and legal mandates.
 
 
 
• **Non-Statutory Bodies:**
 
 
• These are established through executive orders or resolutions without legislative backing.
 
• Examples include the National Commission for Farmers and various advisory committees.
 
• Such bodies primarily serve consultative or advisory roles.
 
 
 
• **National Human Rights Commission (NHRC):**
 
 
• Established in 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993.
 
• It is a statutory body tasked with protecting and promoting human rights.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (NCST):**
 
 
• Established in 2004 under Article 338A of the Indian Constitution.
 
• It is a statutory body dedicated to safeguarding the rights of Scheduled Tribes.
 
 
 
• **National Commission for Women (NCW):**
 
 
• Established in January 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
 
• It is a statutory body focused on ensuring the welfare and rights of women in India.
